title: Burrata with Blistered Tomatoes & Basil Oil
short: Warm, jammy tomatoes against cold, creamy burrata. Ready in 15 minutes.
keywords: Burrata with Blistered Tomatoes & Basil Oil, date night, dinner for two, playful, classic
intro: Burrata is mozzarella's indulgent cousin: a thin shell of fresh cheese filled with cream and soft curds. Tear it open at the table next to warm blistered tomatoes and a bright basil oil and you have a starter that feels generous and takes almost no skill.
why: The moment you tear the burrata open at the table is pure theater, and it is impossible to get wrong.

ings.h: 1 (4 oz)
250 g (9 oz)

steps.t: Take the burrata out of the fridge 20 minutes before serving so it is cool, not cold.
Make the basil oil: pound or finely chop the basil with 2 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add the tomatoes and cook, shaking the pan, for 4–5 minutes until the skins blister and a few burst.
Add the garlic and chili for the last 30 seconds. Take off the heat and stir in the balsamic and a pinch of salt.
Set the burrata in the middle of a shallow plate, spoon the warm tomatoes around it, drizzle with basil oil and finish with flaky salt and pepper. Serve with the toast and tear it open together.

tips: Use the best olive oil you have here; it is a raw ingredient.
If basil is out of season, use a spoon of good pesto loosened with oil.
makeahead: Make the basil oil up to a day ahead; it keeps its color best covered in the fridge.
plating: A shallow, dark plate makes the white burrata pop. Leave space around the edge.
wine: Dry Provençal rosé or a light Italian red served slightly chilled.
zero: Sparkling water with a basil leaf and lemon.

faq.a: Yes. Use fresh buffalo mozzarella torn into pieces; it is less creamy but still lovely.
